questions.stem: A right-angled isosceles triangle \(OPQ\) has its right angle at \(Q\), with \(OQ=PQ=4\). Let \(\mathbf p=\overrightarrow{OP}\) and \(\mathbf q=\overrightarrow{OQ}\). Find \(\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf q\).
questions.hint: Use \(\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf q=|\mathbf p||\mathbf q|\cos\theta\), where \(\theta=\angle POQ\).

keyPoints.note: The two equal legs meet at Q; use Pythagoras for the hypotenuse OP.
The included \angle is at O, between OP and OQ.

steps.explain: The equal legs are 4 and 4, so use Pythagoras to find the hypotenuse OP.

questions.stem: A remote-controlled toy boat moves at 6 m/s in still water. A 2 m/s wind blows from the south-west towards the north-east, and a 5 m/s current flows south. Amelia steers east across an 80 m wide lake. Let \(\mathbf i\) represent 1 m/s east and \(\mathbf j\) represent 1 m/s north. Show that the resultant velocity is \((6+\sqrt2)\mathbf i+(\sqrt2-5)\mathbf j\) m/s.
questions.answer: Sample answer: The wind components are \(2\cos45^circ\mathbf i+2\sin45^circ\mathbf j=\sqrt2\mathbf i+\sqrt2\mathbf j\). The boat velocity is (6\mathbf i) and the current is (-5\mathbf j). Adding gives ((6+\sqrt2)\mathbf i+(\sqrt2-5)\mathbf j) m/s.
questions.hint: Resolve the wind along east and north first. A southward current has a negative j-component.

keyPoints.text: A 2 m/s wind blows from the south-west towards the north-east
keyPoints.note: Resolve this 45° wind into equal positive east and north components.
South is the negative j direction.

steps.explain: The wind points north-east, 45° above east. Resolve it into perpendicular components.

questions.stem: In right-angled triangle \(ABC\), the right angle is at \(B\), and \(M\) is the midpoint of \(AC\). Given \(\overrightarrow{AM}=\mathbf a\) and \(\overrightarrow{BM}=\mathbf b\), find \(\overrightarrow{AB}\) and \(\overrightarrow{BC}\).
questions.hint: Use the route addition rule through M, paying attention to the direction of each vector.

steps.explain: To travel from A to B, go from A to M and then M to B.
Because M is the midpoint of AC, the directed vectors from A to M and M to C are equal.
To travel from B to C, go through M.

questions.stem: In right-angled triangle ABC, the right angle is at B, and M is the midpoint of AC. Given \(\overrightarrow{AM}=\mathbf{a}\) and \(\overrightarrow{BM}=\mathbf{b}\), use vectors to prove that M is equidistant from A, B and C.
questions.answer: Sample answer: \(MA=MB=MC\). Since \(\overrightarrow{AB}=\mathbf{a}-\mathbf{b}\) and \(\overrightarrow{BC}=\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}\), perpendicularity at B gives \((\mathbf{a}-\mathbf{b})\cdot(\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b})=0\), hence \(|\mathbf{a}|^2=|\mathbf{b}|^2\). Also \(MA=MC=|\mathbf{a}|\), as M is the midpoint of AC, and \(MB=|\mathbf{b}|\). Therefore all three distances are equal.
questions.hint: Express the two sides meeting at B as vectors in terms of a and b. Then use the right angle as a zero dot product.

keyPoints.note: Use the perpendicular sides meeting at B to make a zero dot product.

keyPoints.text: M is the midpoint of AC
keyPoints.note: The midpoint gives equal lengths MA and MC.

steps.explain: From the midpoint and vector route rules, write the vectors along the two perpendicular sides.
